newsitem.title: USA: Rubin undoubtedly to stay US Treasury chief - Bowles.
newsitem.headline: Rubin undoubtedly to stay US Treasury chief - Bowles.

text.p: Incoming White House chief of staff Erskine Bowles said Thursday there was no doubt in his mind Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin would remain in his post.

Speaking to reporters after President Bill Clinton named his new national security team, Bowles said he was also likely to name the economic team as group because the "chemistry" among them was important.

He said cited the team as including the treasury, commerce and labor secretaries as well as the head of the council of economic advisers and of the Small Business Administration, a job which Bowles previously held.
Asked if there was any doubt at all that Rubin would stay on, as is widely expected, Bowles replied: "Not to my mind."
Another key job is the chairman of the National Economic Council, which coordinates the administration's economic policy.

The Wall Street Journal on Thursday reported that Clinton was leaning toward naming Tyson's current deputy Gene Sperling and Daniel Tarullo, the White House "sherpa" who prepares Group of Seven summit meetings, to share the job.

Bowles, a former investment banker, said that he had seen instances in his business carreer where co-chairmen worked well together but did not comment on the report. Earlier, a White House spokesman declined comment on the matter.
Aside from the economic team, Bowles said Clinton is likely to name the rest of the Cabinet "piece-meal," adding that the aim was to have made decisions on the Cabinet spots by the end of the year.
